title: Containment: even/odd/ambiguous-depth path-system program ⊆ every set closed under the basic path-system rules
explanation: The Datalog programs classify the nodes a Cook path system (unary axioms A, ternary rules R(x,y,z) meaning x is accessible if y and z both are) makes accessible, by the parity of their derivation trees' leaf depths: EH, OH and AH hold for a node with a derivation whose leaves are all at even depth, all at odd depth, or mixed, respectively. The precondition says a free relation Closed already contains every axiom and is closed under the path-system rule (a pre-fixpoint); the postcondition says the three depth-parity outputs are each contained in Closed. Since Closed ranges over every such closed set and the accessible-node relation is the least one, this is the standard least-fixpoint-containment argument, applied to three refinements of the accessible set at once.
preInWords: PRE says Closed contains every axiom A(x) and is closed under the path-system rule: whenever R(x,y,z) holds and y and z are both already in Closed, x is too.
postInWords: POST says the even-depth, odd-depth and mixed-depth output relations AH, EH and OH are each contained in Closed.

programs.reference: path_systems_basic (its pre-fixpoints are the free relation Closed)

notes: EH/OH/AH classify derivation trees of the path system by leaf-depth parity (all even / all odd / mixed); with the (AH,AH) rule present their union is exactly the accessible set T of path_systems_basic. path_systems_height_old.dl lacks that rule and would make the reverse containment T ⊆ EH ∪ OH ∪ AH false.

The claim is the containment direction only (outputs ⊆ every closed set, i.e. ⊆ T). The reverse direction can be stated as a postcondition on the computed union U = AH ∪ EH ∪ OH: A ∪ π[0](σ(R × U × U)) ⊆ U (U is closed), which by least-fixpoint introduction gives T ⊆ U. Not yet added.

The case was reworked after Val Tannen's Part 1 review questioned the original formulation: 'Is this formulation correct? What does it compute? KEEP SEPARATE TO BE FIXED'. The rework is a bijective renaming of the relation names (`RX` to `R`, `R` to `Closed`, `Ta`/`Tb`/`Tc` to `AH`/`EH`/`OH` and `Sa`/`Sb`/`Sc` to `AHNext`/`EHNext`/`OHNext`), one rule per line with its Datalog reading, and an explanatory header; the precondition, command and postcondition are token-identical to the original under that rename map, checked by script, and the file elaborates.

datalog.label: rules as stated in the header comment of Input.lean
datalog.text:
T(x) :- A(x).
T(x) :- R(x,y,z), T(y), T(z).
EH(x) :- A(x). x has a derivation whose leaves all lie at even depth
OH(x) :- R(x,y,z), EH(y), EH(z). ... all at odd depth
EH(x) :- R(x,y,z), OH(y), OH(z).
AH(x) :- R(x,y,z), Y(y), Z(z) for every other pair (Y,Z) over EH/OH/AH:
